newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end weaker but off lows ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end weaker but off lows ahead of CPI.

text.p: * NZ shares recover from early weakness in afternoon trade
* Volumes remain light
* Market expecting better CPI number than RBNZ
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
306 -1 * NZSC cap index -21.10 at 4,930.48

New Zealand share prices ended softer on Monday but off their lows after a partial rebound in afternoon trade.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index closed 5.88 points down at 2,227.10 after being as low as 2,216.92.
Brokers said early weakness on the back of Wall Street's 2.3 percent plunge late last week was soaked up in afternoon trade, with Tuesday's Consumer Price Index expected to be positive for equities.
"The market is picking below what the Reserve Bank is forecasting," Tim Koller at Merrill Lynch said of the March quarter CPI number, due for release at 10.45 a.m. (2245 GMT).
"If it comes in better, then you should see rates come down, which will help the (equity) market."
The Reserve Bank has forecast core inflation at 0.5 percent in the March quarter, while economists polled by Reuters on average expect 0.41 percent.
Brokers said shares had recovered well in late trade in the face of aggressive selling on Wall Street on Friday.
"It shows that there is good demand for New Zealand stocks," said Koller.
"We don't feel that with the continued shakeout and retreat of the Dow Jones that the New Zealand market needs to follow accordingly."
Most leading stocks closed unchanged to a cent weaker.
Telecom and Fletcher Paper led the recovery, clawing their way back to flat positions after being several cents weaker for most of the session. Telecom ended at NZ$6.48 and FCL Paper at $2.89.
-- Matthew Brockett, Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 473-3736
